kicker: Cement · EBITDA margin change, Q2 FY27
title: Cement sold more; fuel costs took the margin
dek: 11 of 13 listed cement makers lost margin in Q2, 8 of them while selling more, as fuel rose and prices sagged. UltraTech, a top Nifty gainer on 20 Nov, puts October prices 5% above its Q2 average.

read: Demand held up; Q3 margins turn on whether ₹10–20 bag price rises outpace fuel that several makers expect to cost more again.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; market move: HDFC Sky, 20 Nov 2026
notes: Margins are operating EBITDA over revenue from operations in filed Q2 FY27 and Q2 FY26 results (consolidated, except standalone for JK Cement, JSW Cement, Heidelberg India, Orient Cement, Mangalam), as computed by Vantage; company-reported margins can differ, and calls gave no year-ago EBITDA per tonne, so margins are shown. The 13 are every listed cement maker worth ₹2,000 crore or more with clean results; Grasim is left out because it is a diversified holding company. 11 of 13 lost margin (median -4.1 points), 8 of them while sales grew by more than 1% (Ambuja's sales were flat); the two gainers are India Cements, now part of UltraTech, and Prism Johnson, which also makes tiles and ready-mix concrete. Causes are from Q2 FY27 calls: Ambuja's blended fuel cost rose to ₹1.87 per 1,000 kcal from ₹1.60 (ACC and Orient are covered by the Ambuja group call), UltraTech's fuel cost rose to ₹51.5 a bag from ₹45 in one quarter, Dalmia and JSW Cement reported lower realisation (price per tonne) quarter on quarter, and Birla Corp expects fuel to add about ₹100 a tonne in Q3. News hook: UltraTech was among the top Nifty gainers on 20 Nov 2026 (HDFC Sky); its Q2 call is in our data but its filed Q2 results are not, so it is not on the chart; Ramco, Heidelberg and Mangalam had no Q2 call in our data, so no cause is stated for them.
